criteria: open source, D3D12, buildable with the toolchain already verified here (MSVC v145 and the Windows SDK 10.0.26100) without installing anything new
a repeatable workload: deterministic, or fixable to a deterministic step count
GPU-bound enough that the pass under study is measurable on an RX 6950 XT
structurally different from ModelViewer/Sponza: NOT a forward-plus per-light pixel shading loop over a static mesh scene
small enough to build, instrument and measure inside this session's budget
chosen WITHOUT first checking whether it contains a shader already known to be easy to optimise

rejected.too_small_or_not_gpu_bound: D3D12HelloWorld, Fullscreen, Bundles, DynamicIndexing, PipelineStateCache, PredicationQueries, SmallResources, ReservedResources, Residency, 11On12, On7, HDR, DepthBoundsTest, LinkedGpus, xGPU, HeterogeneousMultiadapter, StateObjectDatabase, AdvancedShaderDelivery, SM6WaveIntrinsics
rejected.too_large_for_the_budget: the other D3D12Raytracing samples, and the FidelityFX-SDK sample framework (the local clone is sparse and has no host)
rejected.closed_source: 3DMark Steel Nomad, which is installed and would otherwise qualify on GPU load

selection.why: an O(N^2) n-body simulation: one compute shader, 10 000 particles, LDS tiling, no textures, no lighting, no light grid. Deterministic given a fixed step count. The closest thing to the opposite of the workload 2O and 2P studied.

mass_hoist.equivalence: mass factors out of every term of the sum, including the negative-count correction term, so the two forms are mathematically identical. They are NOT bitwise identical: the rounding happens in a different order, which is exactly why the compiler is not allowed to do it.
mass_hoist.expectation: removes one VALU multiply from each of the ~10 000 interactions per thread

lds_float3.equivalence: only the xyz components of sharedPos were ever read; w was written and never used. The same values reach the same arithmetic in the same order, so the result must be bit-identical.
lds_float3.expectation: 25 % less LDS per group and one fewer dword written per tile

unroll4.equivalence: the same 128 interactions in the same order; only how many of them the compiler sees at once changes. Bit-identical.
unroll4.expectation: fewer live values, so fewer VGPRs and more waves in flight

all3.equivalence: the three above applied together; measured, never assumed to compose
all3.expectation: not assumed to be the sum of the three

criteria.provenance: every build is gated on the compute shader's preregistered bytecode SHA-256; the pristine source is restored on every exit path
criteria.correctness: the particle buffer after a fixed number of deterministic simulation steps, compared at float32 against the baseline's. Baseline vs baseline must be byte-identical first, or nothing can be judged
criteria.performance: median dispatch time from a timestamp pair on the compute queue, recorded per iteration after a warm-up, with several independent processes and counterbalanced order
criteria.acceptance: median delta <= -max(1 %, 3 x N95) with N95 from the baseline A/A control measured in the cycle, every paired process negative, and correctness passing
